examples.name: The Rieger–Nishimura ladder
examples.description: Rieger and Nishimura introduced this construction to study free Heyting algebras on one generator. In particular, the ladder displayed here is the Esakia dual to this algebra.

examples.name: Fine general frame
examples.description: K. Fine introduced this frame to study incompleteness of S4 logics. V. Shehtman later adapted it to obtain an incomplete superintuitionistic logic. It has served as a useful source of counterexamples: for instance, G. Bezhanishvili, D. Gabelaia, and M. Jibladze employed it in their negative solution to Kuznetsov’s problem for bi-Heyting algebras.

examples.name: Mardaev frames
examples.description: The dual algebras were introduced to study pre-locally tabular superintuitionistic logics and to prove that there are continuum many of them.

examples.name: WB graph frame
examples.description: This frame was introduced in our studies of pre-local tabularity and local tabularity, seeking a width-bounded locally tabular logic: it is not locally tabular, but all finitely generated algebras of bounded width in its variety are finite. Every finitely generated algebra in this variety is co-Hopfian.

examples.name: Young lattice Fine frame
examples.description: Young's lattice of partitions was introduced by A. Young in the study of integer partitions in combinatorics and number theory. This particular construction models the Fine general frame, and replaces its "kernel" (the bottom ascending part) by Young's lattice of partitions, obtaining interesting properties.
examples.reference_blurb: This frame arose in our studies of completeness theory, seeking the extent of the Artin-gluing based completion method which was found to work for the Fine general frame.

examples.name: Bellissima’s construction
examples.description: Bellissima’s universal model gives a representation of the free Heyting algebra on two generators by building the "image-finite part" of the dual space. The construction is recursive, and proceeds by layers, taking into account the structure of successors and the "colors" -- the propositional variables satisfied by each point.

examples.motivation_html:
Bellissima’s universal model gives a representation of the free Heyting algebra on two generators by building the "image-finite part" of the dual space. The construction is recursive, and proceeds by layers, taking into account the structure of successors and the "colors" -- the propositional variables satisfied by each point.

Bellissima’s universal model U(2) is the image-finite part part of X2. We begin with four maximal points, one of each colour ∅, {p}, {q}, {p,q}.

At each round we build a new layer of U(2) as follows: pick a finite antichain A from the existing model, containing at least one point from the preceding layer, and a color C which is below the color of each point in this antichain; then add a point which has A as its successors, and is colored C.

The interactive display shows the four maximal points, and a selection of 18 points (the layers grow extremely quickly -- at the third layer several hundreds or thousands of points). The color upsets in the end are given by the points sharing the colors p and q.

At the end of the construction, the poset will contain a copy of each (irreducible) 2-generated Kripke model.

examples.name: Modified Rieger-Nishimura ladder
examples.description: A modified Rieger-Nishimura ladder with an added point on top.
examples.reference_blurb: This simple modification of the RN-ladder can be obtained as a p-morphic image of it, and appears recurringly in studies of completeness: in degrees of FMP, pre-local tabularity, amongst other places.

examples.name: Countable fork
examples.description: An order on the space omega+1, placing the compactification point on the bottom. Simple example of Priestley space which is not Esakia.

examples.name: Countable co-fork
examples.description: An order on the space omega+1, placing the compactification point on the top. An Esakia space which is not bi-Esakia.

examples.name: Deleted top 2-chain space
examples.description: The space $\omega\times 2_{\leq}$ with the upper set of isolated points deleted. Another example of a Priestley space that is not Esakia.

properties.name: Priestley space
properties.description: Compact Hausdorff space where for each pair of points x,y where x is not below y, there is a clopen upset U where x is in U and y is not in U.

properties.name: Esakia space
properties.description: Compact Hausdorff Priestley space in which the downset of every clopen set is clopen.

properties.name: At most countable
properties.description: The underlying set is finite or countably infinite. This concerns the whole construction, including its limit points, rather than the finite diagram window.

properties.name: Finite
properties.description: The underlying set has finitely many points. Finite windows used to draw an infinite construction do not make this property true.

properties.name: Rooted
properties.description: The order has a least element: a point below every point of the space or frame.

properties.name: Noetherian
properties.description: The order has no infinite strictly ascending chain. A nonisolated least point may have transfinite depth without violating this condition.

properties.name: Finite width
properties.description: There is a finite uniform bound on the cardinalities of antichains in the order. For a space or poset, it is assumed only locally: for each rooted upset.

properties.name: Greatest element
properties.description: The order has a greatest element: a point above every point of the space or frame.

properties.name: Isolated root
properties.description: The order has a least element and that point is isolated in the topology.

properties.name: Discrete
properties.description: The topology is discrete (for posets with no specified topology, this is assumed).

properties.name: bi-Esakia space
properties.description: Both the space and its order-dual are Esakia spaces.

properties.name: Finite depth
properties.description: There is a uniform bound on the cardinality of the chains in the order.

properties.name: Clopen maximum
properties.description: The maximum of the space is a clopen set.

properties.name: KM space
properties.description: For every clopen subset, the maximum of the clopen is again clopen.

properties.name: Extremally order-disconnected
properties.description: The upset of the closure of a union of clopen upsets is again a clopen upset.

properties.name: Extremally disconnected
properties.description: Closure of a union of opens is open.

properties.name: Finite incomparability degree
properties.description: For every point in the order, there are finitely many points which are incomparable to it.
